subject: Model shortlist, traffic profile, and next steps for Cortex Health onboarding
messages:
From: Rafael Soto <rafael.soto@cortexhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example.com>, Marta Li <marta.li@cortexhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff — model & traffic details we promised

Mina — thanks again for the quick demo last week. As we prep for the implementation kickoff, wanted to share Cortex Health's expected usage profile so you can recommend a model shortlist and a rough Sizing estimate before our meeting. High level: 
- Primary feature: summarization + clinical QA on notes (both ingest + retrieval-augmented prompts)
- Avg request payload: ~350 tokens in prompt (after retrieval), target reply ~150 tokens
- Concurrent users: start ~40 (beta) -> 400 peak in 6 months
- Avg requests per active user per day: 7 (mostly short Q&A)
- Expected seq lengths: we think retrieval will push effective context windows to 2k–3k tokens for many flows
- Latency target: p95 < 400ms for interactive UX

Attached a sample of typical queries and a short CSV with traffic slices (cortex_sample_queries.csv). Can you and the team propose 2–3 model candidates (tradeoffs: cost vs. latency vs. context) and a horizon-level token-volume estimate? We want something we can show our engineering and procurement teams before the kickoff.

Also flag any constraints around PHI handling / private deployment that affect model selection.

Thanks,
Rafael
VP Product, Cortex Health

----
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example.com>
To: Rafael Soto <rafael.soto@cortexhealth.com>
Cc: Marta Li <marta.li@cortexhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff — model & traffic details we promised

Rafael — great context, thanks for the CSV — that helps a lot. High-level reply up front: we'll propose a short list with one low-latency option, one balanced cost/quality option, and one high-quality/context-optimized option. Notes below are initial estimates; I'll follow up with an internal sizing workbook (attached: initial-sizing-estimate.xlsx) and a short set of throughput projections.

Model shortlist (initial):
- Redwood-8B-Prod (quantized / 8-bit): low-latency, good for short Q&A and cheap inference; effective for <1.5k contexts.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B-Long (16k-window variant): balanced cost, supports longer context up to ~8k — good if retrieval chunks + prompt push you beyond 2k.
- Llama-3-13B-QLoRA (high quality, ~32k-context): best quality on clinical nuance but higher cost per token / higher latency. Use for prioritized workflows (final summaries, clinician-facing outputs).

Context & batching recommendations:
- Retrieval: canonicalize to 1–3 chunks of ~512 tokens each; aim to keep prompts <1.5–2k where possible.
- KV cache & prefix caching: enable for interactive sessions to avoid re-encoding static context repeatedly.
- Batching: target batching window of 10–20ms for interactive UX; larger batch windows for async bulk jobs.

Token-volume quick math (ballpark):
- Start (beta): 40 concurrent users, 7 req/day each -> ~280 requests/day. Assuming average 500 total tokens per request (prompt + completion) -> 140k tokens/day (~4.2M tokens/month).
- 6-month ramp (400 concurrent users): 400*7 = 2,800 req/day * 500 tokens = 1.4M tokens/day (~42M tokens/month).

Latency: with Redwood-8B-Prod we expect p95 ~200–350ms with modest batching; Mistral-Instruct-7B-Long will be ~300–500ms; Llama-3-13B-QLoRA likely ~500–900ms unless served on dedicated capacity.

Security note: because you'll be handling PHI, if you want Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) we should surface that early. Model availability and quantization vary across deployment modes; I'll call out any model that's only available on Dedicated/Private in the follow-up workbook.

Action items (next steps):
- I'll circulate a short workbook with per-model throughput curves + cost projections (attached).
- Laura — can you confirm procurement timeline and any required contract terms so we can align the SOW?
- Neha — can you validate the 2k–3k context flows for retrieval and flag whether we should prioritize the long-window Mistral or Llama path?

Proposed meeting: 11 Oct (week of Oct 11) — 30 mins to review shortlist + SOW draft. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: initial-sizing-estimate.xlsx (contains per-model throughput vs batch size tabs)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL — Cortex Health: sizing ask + who owns which deliverable

Team — looping you in with Rafael's traffic CSV and my initial notes (see thread above). Quick plan and asks so we can finalize the workbook before I send it to Cortex on Friday: 

1) Neha — can you run a throughput sim for: Redwood-8B-Prod (8-bit), Mistral-Instruct-7B-Long (8k), and Llama-3-13B-QLoRA (16k) with the following inputs?
  - request size distribution: 60% small (<300 tokens), 30% medium (300–1,000 tokens), 10% large (>1,000 tokens)
  - target p95 latency <= 400ms for interactive flows
  - concurrency scenarios: beta (40 concurrent), month-6 (400 concurrent)
  Please add recommended batch windows and expected GPU count for dedicated pools where appropriate.

2) Laura — procurement / contract checkpoint: Rafael mentioned procurement review next week. Can you confirm if a 60-day SOC2 evidence window + standard Data Processing Addendum is sufficient? Also confirm billing cadence they prefer (monthly vs quarterly).

3) Monica — please draft a short onboarding checklist for Cortex (data ingestion, retrieval index best practices, PHI controls) that we can share in the kickoff packet.

Deliverable timeline: internal sim + updated workbook by Fri EOD (8 Oct). Mina will send workbook + calendar invite for 11 Oct once we have the numbers.

Thanks — I'll merge your outputs into the sizing workbook. Quote from Rafael below for context.

> "Primary feature: summarization + clinical QA on notes (both ingest + retrieval-augmented prompts). Avg request payload: ~350 tokens in prompt (after retrieval), target reply ~150 tokens."

Mina

- Also please note any model variants that would require Dedicated/Private (for PHI).

Looking forward to the 11 Oct call.

Best,
Rafael
